name: Astra DB
summary: DataStax’s serverless database built on Apache Cassandra, run on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, with CQL tables, a JSON Data API and vector search; part of IBM since 2025.
intro: Astra DB Serverless runs Cassandra for you on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure. You create a database in a region and get keyspaces and tables as in Cassandra, reachable with CQL through the usual Cassandra drivers and a CQL shell. There is also a Data API, with clients for Python, TypeScript, Java, Go and C#, that treats a table as a collection of JSON documents with a flexible schema, and can sort results by similarity to a `$vector`. Indexes are Storage Attached Indexes (SAI), which allow filtering on non-key columns.

DataStax manages the cluster settings. Each region keeps three replicas across three availability zones, and a database can add regions, with data streamed from the primary region and arriving everywhere eventually. Writes at `ANY`, `ONE` and `LOCAL_ONE` are refused. Only the Unified Compaction Strategy is used, `cassandra.yaml` can’t be changed, and `nodetool` and JMX tools aren’t available. Limits include 200 tables and 100 indexes per database, 10 indexes per table, 75 columns per table and around 12,000 operations a second before rate limiting.

DataStax launched Astra as a hosted Cassandra service in May 2020 and re-engineered it in 2021 into a serverless service whose storage is separated from compute, billed by use. IBM announced it would buy DataStax in February 2025 and closed the deal in May; Astra DB is now sold within IBM watsonx, next to DataStax Enterprise, the self-managed Hyper-Converged Database (HCD) and Langflow.
strengths: Cassandra’s data model and drivers without running the cluster, on any of the three big clouds
One database for CQL tables, JSON document collections and vector search
Multi-region databases and a free plan for small projects
Zero Downtime Migration tooling for moving existing Cassandra clusters
limits: Tight per-database limits: 200 tables, 100 indexes, about 10 Data API collections
No access to cluster settings, compaction strategy or `nodetool`; replication is fixed at three per region
Multi-region replication is eventually consistent and can lag for hours during failures
The free plan allows five databases, without private endpoints or multi-region replication

goodFor.why: The Data API sorts a collection by similarity to a `$vector`, next to CQL tables in the same database.
Serverless since 2021, with storage separated from compute and billing by use, plus a free plan for small projects.

specs.data-model: Cassandra tables, plus JSON document collections through the Data API
specs.query-language: CQL, and the JSON Data API
specs.wire-protocol: Cassandra drivers (CQL); Data API clients for Python, TypeScript, Java, Go and C#
specs.secondary-indexes: Storage Attached Indexes (SAI), up to 10 per table
specs.replication: Three replicas across three availability zones per region
specs.multi-region: Regions can be added; replication between them is eventually consistent
specs.storage-engine: Cassandra, with the Unified Compaction Strategy only
specs.deployment: Managed only, on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure
specs.pricing: Serverless, billed by use; free plan up to five databases

story: DataStax was founded in 2010, as Riptano, by Jonathan Ellis and Matt Pfeil to sell support for Apache Cassandra, and in 2011 it released DataStax Enterprise, a commercial Cassandra distribution. In May 2020 it launched Astra, a database service that ran Cassandra clusters in the cloud for customers.

In February 2021 DataStax announced a serverless version, generally available that March: it re-engineered the storage tier so it was separate from compute nodes, which let databases grow and shrink without a set size and bill only for what they used. Vector search followed in 2023, turning Astra DB into a vector store for AI applications alongside its Cassandra workloads.

IBM announced in February 2025 that it would acquire DataStax for its Astra DB, DataStax Enterprise and Langflow products, and closed the acquisition in May 2025. The products now sit in IBM’s watsonx portfolio, and the documentation carries IBM’s branding.

choices.why: Classic Cassandra ties data to the nodes that serve it, so capacity is bought in nodes. Splitting the two let Astra scale each on its own and charge by use instead of by cluster size.

choices.choice: A JSON Data API on top of CQL tables
choices.why: Fixed-schema tables suit structured rows, while collections with a dynamic schema suit semi-structured JSON and vectors. The Data API offers both over the same storage, so not every app has to design Cassandra tables.

choices.choice: Fixed replication of three across zones
choices.why: DataStax sets the replication factor (three, with `NetworkTopologyStrategy`) and the compaction strategy itself and doesn’t let users change them, so every database is equally durable and maintenance can run region by region on a schedule.

timeline.text: Riptano, later DataStax, is founded to support Cassandra
Astra launches as a cloud Cassandra service in May
Serverless Astra DB, with storage separated from compute, becomes generally available
Vector search comes to Astra DB
IBM announces in February and completes in May its acquisition of DataStax
